cohort: The study included antipsychotic-naive first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients and healthy controls from two independent samples (Barcelona and Santander).
finding: Antipsychotic-naive FEP patients were shorter, slimmer, and had lower BMI compared to controls, with winter birth and lower birth weight influencing height, especially in female patients and males respectively, at the onset of FEP.
cross-section timing: Anthropometric measurements were taken at the onset of first-episode psychosis.
birth_weight: Measured as an exposure; no specific range mentioned for inclusion criteria.
